 Nearly 4,000 Bottles of Blood Pressure Medication Recalled Nationwide, FDA Warns 
 Nearly 4,000 Bottles of Blood Pressure Medication Recalled Nationwide, FDA Warns 
 Here’s how to tell if your meds are affected.
 By Jenn Gonick Published: Nov 03, 2026 10:47 AM EST Save Article Share Article Science Photo Library // Getty Images 2 min read Key Points 
 3,700 bottles of a popular blood pressure medication have been recalled nationwide, according to the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA).
 The recalled meds “failed dissolution specifications.”
 Here’s how to tell if your meds are affected.
 If you take medication to help manage your blood pressure , you may want to take a second look at the label. Nearly 4,000 bottles of blood pressure medication have been recalled nationwide, according to the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA).
 According to the FDA’s announcement , the voluntary recall was initiated by Macleods Pharma USA, Inc. on October 7 because the meds “failed dissolution specifications.” That means the drug may be ineffective, as the active ingredients may not release inside the body at the proper rate.
 On October 26, the FDA gave the recall a Class II designation, which means that taking the affected meds “may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.” Here’s what you need to know.
 Which products are affected by the recall?
 The recall affects 3,528 30-count bottles and 216 90-count bottles of olmesartan medoxomil, Amlodipine, and Hydrochlorothiazide Tablets (a generic of the brand Tribenzor). Check your medicine cabinet for the following information:
 Olmesartan Medoxomil, Amlodipine, and Hydrochlorothiazide Tablets 40 mg/10 mg/12.5 mg, 30-count 
 Add Prevention as a preferred source in your Google search results. Use your Google account to add this to your settings. Add to Google settings NDC: 33342-246-07 
 Lot number: 12251163A
 Expiration date: May 31, 2027
 Olmesartan Medoxomil, Amlodipine, and Hydrochlorothiazide Tablets 40 mg/10 mg/12.5 mg, 90-count 
 NDC: 33342-246-10
 Lot number: 12251163B
 Expiration date: May 31, 2027
 More information can be found in the FDA’s enforcement report .
 What should you do with a recalled product?
 As of right now, the FDA hasn’t issued specific instructions to consumers. However, if you do have any of the recalled blood pressure meds in your home, you should contact the doctor who prescribed them to you before discontinuing use. If you’ve been taking the recalled pills and have any health concerns, talk with your doctor.
